examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Value of an Observation, Standard Deviation, or Mean Given a Z-Score
examples.problem: A data set has a standard deviation $\sigma=1.2$ and an unknown mean. An observation of the data set has the value $x=13.2$ and $z$-score $z=-1.5.$ Find the mean of the data set.
examples.worked_solution:
To compute the value of an observation $x$ which yields a given $z$-score in a data set with mean $\overline{x}$ and standard deviation $\sigma,$ we can use the following formula:

$$
x = \overline{x} + z \cdot \sigma
$$

Substituting $x=13.2,$ $z=-1.5,$ and $\sigma=1.2$ into the formula and solving for $\overline{x}$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\overset{―}{x}+z\cdot \sigma  \\ 13.2 & =\overset{―}{x}+(-1.5)\cdot 1.2 \\ 13.2 & =\overset{―}{x}-1.8 \\ \overset{―}{x} & =13.2+1.8 \\ \overset{―}{x} & =15\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
The $z$-score of an observation $x$ is defined by

$$
z=\frac{x-\overset{―}{x}}{\sigma }.
$$

The $z$-score represents how many standard deviations an observation is above or below the mean of the data set.

Here, we're told that the mean is $\overset{―}{x}=-1.2,$ and we can calculate the standard deviation as

$$
\sigma =\sqrt{{\sigma }^{2}}=\sqrt{0.32}.
$$

So, the $z$-score of the observation $x=-2.1$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =\frac{x-\overset{―}{x}}{\sigma } \\  & =\frac{-2.1-(-1.2)}{\sqrt{0.32}} \\  & ≈-1.59,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $2$ decimal places.
